page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r5.2xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual server instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped from 4 physical Intel Xeon 8163 cores with hyper-threading enabled, running at a clock speed of 2.5 GHz. The instance is equipped with 64.0 GB of system memory, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, relying entirely on network-attached storage and baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates that the processor architecture, which supports AVX-512 and AES instructions, delivers moderate performance. Passmark CPU and extended instruction tests place the instance in the average tier, while single-core and multi-core stress-ng benchmarks fall into the lower 25% of tested hardware. Memory performance shows a similar split: small-block cached read bandwidth is relatively weak, but large-block uncached read and write operations achieve average tier speeds of 41.01 GB/sec and 35.87 GB/sec respectively. Large-model LLM text generation and single-threaded compression tasks show poor performance, though small-model LLM inference achieves average processing speeds.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the ecs.r5.2xlarge offers a high density of memory resources relative to its compute allocation, making it a viable option for memory-bound workloads that do not require high-frequency CPU performance. Given the lack of local storage and moderate network throughput, it is best suited for caching layers, in-memory databases, and lightweight data processing tasks where memory capacity is the primary bottleneck.

Performance benchmarks show average results for large-block memory bandwidth and Passmark CPU tests, alongside weaker single-core and multi-core processing scores. With a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps, the instance is qualitatively cost-effective for memory-intensive workloads that do not demand extreme compute power. It is well-suited for in-memory databases, caching layers, and general memory-bound applications.
